content: A fitness trail, also known as a par course (derived from the French word parcours, meaning course), is a designated path or route that incorporates various obstacles or exercise stations along its length. These stations are specifically designed to facilitate physical activity and promote overall health and fitness. The concept of the fitness trail is rooted in the physical training philosophy of Georges Hébert. Fitness trails can be constructed using natural or artificial elements and are often located in diverse environments such as forests, transportation corridors, parks, or urban areas. The equipment along these trails is intended to provide targeted forms of physical exercise. Natural features like climbable rocks, trees, or riverbanks may serve as exercise stations, while manufactured equipment such as stepping posts, chin-up bars, and climbing bars can replicate similar physical challenges. The difficulty level of a fitness trail is influenced by several factors, including the slope of the terrain, the type of trail surface (e.g., dirt, grass, or gravel), the height of obstacles (such as walls), the length of certain challenges (like crawling sections), and other design features. Urban fitness trails are typically designed to be flat, making them accessible to older adults and accommodating a variety of users, including cyclists, runners, skaters, and walkers. A modern evolution of the fitness trail is the outdoor gym, which incorporates traditional gym equipment specifically adapted for outdoor use. The concept of the par course originated in 1968, when Swiss architect Erwin Weckemann developed the first such course with the support of a Swiss insurance company. By 1972, hundreds of these courses had been constructed across Europe. In the United States, fitness trails began to emerge in the following years. Notable examples include the Parcour exercise trail established in 1976 at County Farm Park in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and the Bruce Jenner Trail, created in 1977 within the Lake County Forest Preserve District in Illinois. In Hong Kong, the Lion Rock Country Park, featuring 15 exercise stations, was inaugurated in 1977. Examples of fitness trails around the world include the Chernikoff Fitness Trail in Prince George County, Maryland, USA; a maintained list of Parcours Fitness Trails in the Puget Sound area of Washington State, USA; and the Queens Park Fitness Trail in Invercargill, New Zealand. The fitness trail equipment industry has developed standardized multi-station equipment packages to meet the needs of par courses. Several manufacturers specialize in producing such equipment, including Columbia Cascade, Fit Trail, GameTime, Outdoor Fitness Equipment, and TriActive America.
